sources.title: A practical guide to building agents
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-001. Provider guidance supports bounded definitions and incremental design, not universal superiority.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-002. Provider engineering synthesis; architecture recommendations require local tests.

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-013. Bounded vendor case for parallel research; not general multi-agent superiority or cost-effectiveness.

sources.title: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-023. Risk guidance, not a complete engineering standard or assurance result.

sources.title: Operator System Card
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-030. Product-specific confirmation and risk evidence with residual limitations.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-036. Voluntary cross-sector framework; under revision and not an agent runtime or certification.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-037. Cross-sector profile, not agent-specific assurance or sector authorization.

sources.title: Agent Development Kit: Multi-agent systems
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-042. Framework patterns do not establish that multiple agents improve a task.

sources.title: ChatGPT agent system card: user confirmations
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-043. Product-specific confirmation and supervision evidence, not universal authority or safety proof.

sources.title: Running agents
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-003. One SDK demonstrates explicit run-loop branches and limits; the FieldOps state machine remains local and provider-neutral.

sources.title: Tracing
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-040. Provider trace vocabulary is illustrative; traces are evidence pointers, not effect truth.

sources.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-019. Synthetic benchmark evidence for outcome and state checks; scores do not transfer to FieldOps.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-020. Provider evaluation guidance; grader validity and sample sufficiency remain use-case dependent.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25: Tools
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-004. Versioned tool specification; annotations are untrusted unless the server is trusted and protocol conformance does not grant application authority.

sources.title: Writing effective tools for AI agents using AI agents
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-005. Provider engineering findings require local task evaluation.

sources.title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-014. Idempotency requires service support and semantic intent; it neither guarantees exactly once nor reverses effects.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol security best practices
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-024. Protocol guidance does not replace application threat modeling or domain authority.

sources.title: Inside OpenAI's in-house data agent
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-034. Organization-specific vendor case; outcomes are not independently reproduced or transferable.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25: Authorization
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-006. HTTP MCP authorization still requires local task delegation and effect approval semantics.

sources.title: RFC 9700: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-007. OAuth security guidance does not define agent business authority or consent.

sources.title: RFC 8707: Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-008. Resource indicators restrict audience but do not establish least-privilege scope or effect approval.

sources.title: RFC 9728: OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-044. Metadata discovery does not prove resource trust or authorize a business effect.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25: Elicitation
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-009. Elicitation is an interaction primitive, not proof that a named human has formal authority.

sources.title: Human-in-the-loop
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-017. Serializable approval and resume mechanism; authorization quality depends on identity, scope, expiry, and enforcement.

sources.title: Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization
sources.notes: Maps AGE-BSRC-038. Government concept paper only, not a standard, control set, or completed reference architecture.
